_doc: Revert-verify mutants for req 394389b1-fcf8-4af1-962f-fad2b943f0a1 (issue #4527) — the NON-SCALAR guard in `createUpdatePropertyService` (service_call `updateProperty`). ⛔ The subject is in packages/services, which NO workflow jest-runs — the axes therefore live in packages/cli, gated by test-coverage-cli, whose moduleNameMapper resolves @kitelev/exocortex-services to package SOURCE. The harness also runs the req 5d2c7ede suite (W-axes) on purpose: the ORDER of the two guards is load-bearing, so a mutant that removes the empty-value guard must be seen to break BOTH the #4516 wording and this req's control. Set `tree`/`subject` to YOUR checkout before running.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/services/src/grounding-service-factories.ts

M1_guard_not_wired._note: Severs the call to the non-scalar predicate, type-preserving. Reddens every refusal axis of this req; the controls (N6 populated array, N7 scalars, N8 the #4516 wording) and all W-axes stay GREEN — the two predicates do not overlap.

M2_predicate_rejects_any_array._note: The TOO-BROAD predicate: refuse every array instead of only one with a non-scalar element. Reddens the populated-array controls in BOTH suites (N6 here, W5 in the #4516 suite) and nothing else — multi-value writes would have died silently.
M2_predicate_rejects_any_array.to: return "an array with a non-scalar element";

M3_predicate_ignores_array_elements._note: The TOO-NARROW predicate: judge the container only, never its elements. Reddens exactly the two array forms — N4 (`["a",{}]` → `- [object Object]`) and N5 (`[[1]]` → flattened to `- 1`) — while the object forms (N1-N3) stay refused.

M4_message_omits_corruption._note: Keeps the refusal, drops the word the issue's acceptance criterion demands. Reddens every axis that asserts the WORDING (N2 explicitly, N3 and N9 through their /CORRUPT/i matchers) — the second deliverable of this req is the message, not only the refusal.
M4_message_omits_corruption.from: refusing rather than CORRUPTING the key.

M5_empty_guard_removed._note: Removes the req 5d2c7ede guard that must run FIRST. Proves the ORDER is load-bearing and that this guard does NOT substitute for it: `""` is a scalar and `[]` is a (vacuously) scalar array, so both sail through and get WRITTEN (W1, W2, W6 red), while `null` — whose typeof is "object" — is caught here and answered with a CORRUPTION message instead of the clearing one (W4 and this req's control N8 red).

M6_scalar_set_drops_boolean._note: Narrows the scalar set so a BOOLEAN becomes non-scalar. Exists because the five mutants above leave N7 — the control saying every scalar form is still written — reddened by NOTHING: an unproven control is worse than a missing one, since it manufactures confidence (integration-test-revert-verify §A130: the axis exists, the mutant for it does not; NOT §A35 defensive and NOT §A118 a dead condition). Reddens exactly N7 and nothing else: strings and the populated array (N6, W5, W7) stay scalar, so only the boolean sub-case of N7 flips.
M6_scalar_set_drops_boolean.from: typeof v === "string" || typeof v === "number" || typeof v === "boolean";
